scope: The two cars Qazi asked about · Nashville, TN
title: What These 296s Have Been Through
lead: Two 2022 296 GTBs in Rosso Corsa at Prancing Horse of Nashville. Both CARFAX reports and window stickers read line by line; priced against 9 BaT sales and 12 live dealer asks.
takeaway: Newest (Nov 20): McLaren Newport Beach's 3.1k-mile 2022 at $318,966 failed California smog Oct 16 and has an unexplained 850-mile repair list, so it's a pass unless the smog cert and repair order check out; fair is $285k to $295k. My two cents: the 2,862-mile car is the one. Both ask about $330k; BaT has been selling 2022 to 2023 GTBs for $267k to $288k all year. Open the 2.9k car at $318k, land $300k, walk above $305k. Ferrari of Tampa Bay's $309,985 2023 is no lever: its CARFAX shows an Aug 2026 rear-end accident, 4 owners incl. corporate fleet, and it is not CPO. Neither car shows a service since 2023 or 2024, so the service printout comes first.
shift: BaT, Jun 23, 2026 (+5% buyer fee, capped $7,500). Closest match to the 5.3k car
BaT, Jul 20, 2026; newest 2022 to 2023 GTB sale
9 BaT sales of 2022 to 2023 GTBs this year
$267,777 to $327,000, median $275,000 (about $282,500 with the fee). Only the $161k-option matte car and an Assetto Fiorano cleared $300k

Ferrari of Tampa Bay 3k $309,985 (accident Aug 2026, 4 owners, not CPO); Sport Cars Lux 2k $319,990; Ferrari of SF 6k $327,864; Greensboro 6k $329,950; Napleton 5k $330,412; Fort Lauderdale 2k $345,000 (classic.com, Nov 15)

Both cars were delivered new by this store, listed here Sep 27, 2024, sold in 2025 and came back. Neither shows an annual service since 2023 (2.9k) or Apr 2024 (5.3k). The 5.3k car had brakes done at 3,100 mi
sources: Dealer listings, window stickers (dealer Window Sticker button) and free CARFAX reports (ar20 links) read in full in Walt Chrome, Nov 15, 2026. Ferrari Approved page for the 2.9k car. Days listed from the dealer's own in-stock dates (Oct 12 and Nov 7). Sold prices from Bring a Trailer; live asks and market average from classic.com, Nov 15. Reviews: Google (610 of 734, newest first), Yelp, DealerRater, Cars.com, BBB, CarEdge. Staff from phofnash.com/about-us/staff. Nobody contacted.

cars.verdict: Sold Nov 17. Kostas told Qazi on the phone. $24,995 over the $305k cap at $329,995. Open $318k, target $300k, walk above $305k. The better of the two: lowest miles, carbon Corsa seats, ceramic tips, PPF, $412,547 sticker, and 34 days on the lot. The knock: no service reported since Jun 2023. Before money, ask for the Ferrari service printout and the Ferrari Approved inspection, and why it came back.

cars.verdict: Kostas countered $320,000 on Nov 17. Ferrari North America owned it its first 2 years (corporate fleet car), then it sat about 10 months on this lot in 2024-25. $20,995 over the $305k cap at $325,995. Open $314k, target $295k, walk above $300k. BaT sold a 6k-mile Rosso Corsa / Nero 2022 for $275,000 in June. Brakes at 3,100 miles is the question: the 296's rotors are carbon ceramic, so that means track days or a warranty fix. Get the April 2024 repair order before anything else. Only 8 days listed, so less bend than the 2.9k car.

cars.verdict: Cleanest history of the three: 1 owner, 2,025 miles, all Ferrari-dealer service, no accidents. But it has no warranty (ended Mar 2026), no carbon key, no Daytona seats, and the wheels in the photos don't match the matte grey factory wheels on its plaque. 48 days on this lot after failing to sell in Vegas. Their own site says $309,990, so that's the ceiling. First offer $285k, most I'd pay $295k, plus a Ferrari dealer inspection and a 2-year Power extension (about $7k).

cars.verdict: Pass unless they clear three things. $13,966 over the $305k cap at $318,966, with no warranty (ended about Oct 2025) and no Ferrari Approved, since a McLaren store can't certify a Ferrari. 1. Failed California smog Oct 16: a CA dealer must hand over a passing smog certificate, so get it before any money. 2. The 850-mile repair list (A/C compressor, intake manifold, all four calipers) at an independent shop: get that repair order and the reason. 3. Tires twice in 1,500 miles reads like track or hard use. Its paper is worse than the 1-owner Miami car at $309,990. Fair: open $285k, land $292k, walk above $295k.
